subject: Verizon and Comcast Cable License Renewals
overview: The city held a public hearing to gather input on community needs and operator compliance prior to negotiating new cable television licenses for Verizon and Comcast. Officials presented a ten-year capital plan for Medford Community Media and reviewed the legal limitations of the renewal process.

items.title: Opening and Legal Notice
items.summary: Cable Counsel William Hewig opened the hearing and Communications Director Steve Smirti read the official legal notice regarding the renewal of licenses for Verizon and Comcast.

items.title: Overview of Negotiable Cable License Terms
items.summary: Counsel outlined the scope of negotiations, explaining that while rates and broadband services are federally protected, the city will negotiate for public access funding, HD channels, and capital grants.

items.title: License Expiration Dates and Proposed Renewal Terms
items.summary: The hearing established that the Verizon license expires in February 2025 and the Comcast license in July 2025, with proposed renewal terms of five and ten years respectively.

items.title: Medford Community Media Program Presentation
items.summary: Station Manager Kevin Harrington presented a video showcasing the local benefits of Medford Community Media (MCM) and its role in providing city-wide news and creative outlets.

items.title: FY26 Budget and Ten-Year Capital Projections
items.summary: Harrington detailed a preliminary $329,889 fiscal year 2026 budget and a long-term capital plan including studio lighting, camera upgrades, and a potential relocation fund.

items.title: Public Comment and Hearing Closure
items.summary: Counsel closed the public hearing after inviting written testimony on operator compliance and community needs, noting that no members of the public were present to speak.
